messages.subject: timer
messages.body_plain:
I think timer had an incorrect range for wave4. I also improved the
speed by removing a for loop. I pointed at other places where I (or
someone else) could get speed improvements.

fast.timer<-function (wave, f, threshold = 5, envt = "abs", power = 1,
msmooth = NULL,
    ksmooth = NULL, plot = TRUE, plotthreshold = TRUE, col = "black",
    colval = "red", xlab = "Time (s)", ylab = "Amplitude", ...)
{
    if (power == 0)
        stop("'power' cannot equal to 0")
    input <- inputw(wave = wave, f = f)
    wave <- input$w
    f <- input$f
    rm(input)
    n <- length(wave)
    thres <- threshold/100
    wave1 <- env(wave = wave, f = f, msmooth = msmooth, ksmooth =
ksmooth,
        envt = envt, norm = TRUE, plot = FALSE)^power
    n1 <- length(wave1)
    F <- f * (n1/n)
    wave1 <- ts(wave1, start = 0, end = n1/F, freq = F)
    wave2 <- ifelse(wave1 <= thres, yes = 1, no = 2)
    # not used?##  wave3 <- ts(wave2, start = 0, end = n1/F, freq = F)
    # wave4 <- numeric(n1)
    # for (i in 1:(n - 1)) { #should this be for (i in 1:(n1 - 1))?
    #    wave4[i] <- wave2[i] + wave2[i + 1]
    #}
    wave4<-wave2+lag(wave2,k=1) #increase speed? try apply()?
    wave4[1] <- 3
    wave4[n1] <- 3
    wave5 <- which(wave4 == 3)
    n5 <- length(wave5)
    wave6 <- numeric(n5 - 1)
    for (i in 1:(n5 - 1)) {  # potential to increase speed using lag()
or apply()?
        wave6[i] <- wave5[i + 1] - wave5[i]
    }
    y <- wave6/F
    if (wave2[1] == 1) {
        pause <- y[seq(1, n5 - 1, by = 2)]
        signal <- y[seq(2, n5 - 1, by = 2)]
    } else {
        signal <- y[seq(1, n5 - 1, by = 2)]
        pause <- y[seq(2, n5 - 1, by = 2)]
    }
    ratio <- sum(signal)/sum(pause)
    timer <- list(s = signal, p = pause, r = ratio)
    if (plot == TRUE) {
        plot(wave1, xlab = xlab, ylab = ylab, yaxt = "n", xaxt = "n",
            , ylim = c(0, 1 + 0.1), col = col, type = "l", xaxs =
"i",
            ...)
        if (plotthreshold == TRUE) {
            abline(h = thres, col = colval, lty = 2)
            mtext(paste(as.character(threshold), "%"), side = 2,
                line = 0.5, at = thres, las = 1, col = colval,
                cex = 0.8)
        }
        par(new = TRUE)
        plot(wave2, xlab = "", ylab = "", yaxt = "n", type = "l",
            col = colval, ylim = c(1, 2 + 0.1), xaxs = "i", ...)
        wave8 <- numeric(n5 - 1)
        for (i in 2:n5) {
            wave8[i] <- ((wave5[i] - wave5[i - 1])/2) + wave5[i -
                1]
        }
        if (wave2[1] == 1) {
            wave8.1 <- wave8[seq(2, n5, by = 2)]/F
            wave8.2 <- wave8[seq(3, n5, by = 2)]/F
        }  else {
            wave8.2 <- wave8[seq(2, n5, by = 2)]/F
            wave8.1 <- wave8[seq(3, n5, by = 2)]/F
        }
        ypl <- as.character(round(pause, 2))
        ysl <- as.character(round(signal, 2))
        text(x = wave8.1, y = 1.075, ypl, col = colval, cex = 0.8)
        text(x = wave8.2, y = 2.075, ysl, col = colval, cex = 0.8)
        invisible(timer)
    }
    else {
        return(timer)
    }
}

# Jerome, many may thanks for putting this package together

#eal

messages.subject: Re: timer
messages.body_plain:
I just realized that env also uses a for loop that adds time to timer.
If one fixes env() with the following

wave2<-apply(as.matrix(step),1,function(x) mean(wave1[x:(x +
msmooth[1])]))

both env and timer will run orders of magnitude faster.

eal
